name: Clment REST API
description:
The Clment REST API gives your services programmatic access to the
same contract workspace you use in the app — contracts, AI reviews,
rulebooks, key dates, and search.

## Authentication

Every request carries a bearer token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer clm_sk_live_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

Generate a key in the app under **Settings → API & Integrations →
API keys**. The secret is shown **once** at creation — store it in a
secret manager. A key is scoped to the organization it was created
in and inherits that workspace's data residency region.

## What a key can and can't do

An API key can read and write everything a member can in the app:
upload contracts, run reviews, edit rulebooks, manage key dates,
search. It **cannot** touch settings — billing, members, SSO,
integrations, organization config, or webhook subscriptions. Those
require a human admin signed in to the app.

## Regions & base URL

Use your organization's home region's base URL. A key only works
against the region it belongs to — calling another region returns
401. (This is the same list as the **Servers** dropdown above; both
are generated from our live region catalog.)

<!--REGIONS_TABLE_START-->
| Region         | Base URL                       |
|----------------|--------------------------------|
| United States  | `https://api-us.clment.com/v1` |
| European Union | `https://api-eu.clment.com/v1` |
| Australia      | `https://api-au.clment.com/v1` |
| New Zealand    | `https://api-nz.clment.com/v1` |
| United Kingdom | `https://api-uk.clment.com/v1` |
| Canada         | `https://api-ca.clment.com/v1` |
<!--REGIONS_TABLE_END-->

## Response envelope

Successful responses wrap their payload in a `data` object:

```json
{ "data": { "contract": { "id": "…" } } }
```

Errors return an `error` object with a stable machine-readable
`code` and a human `message`:

```json
{ "error": { "code": "NOT_FOUND", "message": "Contract not found" } }
```

## Pagination

List endpoints page with `skip` and `take` (max 100). The response
carries the page plus a `total` count so you can compute whether
more pages remain.

## Long-running operations (jobs)

Uploads, reviews, and redlines run as background jobs. The kick-off
endpoint returns a **job id** immediately; poll the matching job
endpoint until it reports `complete`, then fetch the result.

| Action | Start | Poll | Result |
|--------|-------|------|--------|
| Upload  | `POST /contracts/upload` | `GET /contracts/upload/jobs/{jobId}` | `GET /contracts/{id}` |
| Review  | `POST /contracts/{id}/review` | `GET /jobs/review/{id}` | `GET /reviews/{reviewId}` |
| Redline | `POST /contracts/{id}/generate-redline` | `GET /jobs/redline/{id}` | `GET /contracts/download/{token}` |

An API key always gets the job id back as JSON — the live
Server-Sent Events variant of the review and redline start
endpoints belongs to first-party app sessions. Polling is the
right shape for a server-to-server integration anyway: simpler
than holding a stream open, and it survives the process that
started the job going away.

## Rate limits & credits

Two independent limits apply:

- **Credits.** AI operations (reviews, redlines, conversions) consume
  credits from your plan's monthly allowance, then any credit packs.
  Read operations are free. A `402 INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS` indicates an
  exhausted balance.
- **Request rate.** Requests are rate-limited per organization on a
  rolling hourly window sized to your plan. Every AUTHENTICATED
  response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`
  (the limiter is per-organization, so it runs only once the key has
  resolved to one — a 401 carries neither); exceed the window
  and you get a `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header (in
  seconds) — back off for that long, then retry.

## Plan & access

The API is available on the **Business** and **Enterprise** plans. A
call from an org without API access returns `403 API_ACCESS_NOT_IN_PLAN`;
a call from an org whose subscription has lapsed returns
`403 SUBSCRIPTION_SUSPENDED`. Both clear once the plan or billing
status is resolved in the app (with a short propagation delay). An API
key also can't reach settings surfaces — billing, members, SSO,
integrations, org config, webhooks — which return `403 API_KEY_FORBIDDEN`.

## Versioning

The API is versioned in the path; the current version is `v1` (every
base URL ends `/v1`).

- **Additive changes ship in place:** new endpoints, new optional
  request fields, and new response fields arrive within `v1` without
  notice. Write clients to ignore unknown response fields so these
  never break you.
- **Breaking changes ship under a new path version** (`/v2`) — removing
  or renaming a field, changing a type, or tightening validation. `v1`
  keeps working through a published deprecation window.

The `version` of this document tracks the spec's own revisions.
